definitions.claim_boundary: bounded non-final diagnostic on development/exposed lineages; zero fresh captures; no multi-shot, adaptation, zero-shot, or complete-gameplay claim; cannot reopen #64/#65/#72/#75/#15/#76; the #80/#82/#85 published outcomes are read-only inputs, never re-run, amended, or reinterpreted; descriptive intervals only
definitions.compute_accounting: per decision cell: wall time, perception wall, transition calls, linear MACs, candidate counts, active-parameter counts; per oracle cell: execution wall; candidate count alone is never compute matching; inference is NOT equalized across arms and is recorded as such
definitions.decision_anchor_rule: per state, the sealed pre-decision frame is the decision frame of the state's lowest-ordinal oracle cell that produced a valid executed segment (outcome-blind: selection never reads success/failure); the frame is byte-verified against the shot's first native frame; cross-candidate byte agreement of every executed oracle cell's decision frame is recorded per state; a state with no executed oracle cell is a typed decision failure for all of its system cells
definitions.decision_pass: DECISION-ONLY: per system x seed x state the frozen predictors score the state's candidate inventory (the #85 reactive rule); NO gameplay is executed for system cells; the system's closed-loop outcome is the engine-truth verdict of its chosen candidate from the oracle pass, bound by candidate identity; if the chosen candidate's oracle cell is a typed failure the system cell inherits that typed failure (no success value)
definitions.decision_rule: the #85 reactive decision rule, inherited verbatim: single-frame parse of the sealed pre-decision frame with the frozen issue-70 adapter, roll every admissible candidate to the system's fixed pair, choose argmin predicted count cost with ties broken by lower ordinal; candidates with nonfinite predictions are excluded; the no-model prior arm executes the #82 fallback rule (ordinal 8 when admissible, else the admissible ordinal nearest 8, ties to the lower ordinal); a typed decision failure is terminal and executes no shot

q1_closed_loop_oracle_ceiling_nonzero.not_supported_by_this_experiment: complete execution with oracle prevalence = 0: no admissible candidate succeeded anywhere, a measured state-difficulty floor (a valid null, reported)
q1_closed_loop_oracle_ceiling_nonzero.readiness_or_precision_insufficient: prevalence > 0 but the descriptive interval contains 0 (precision), or the execution inventory is incomplete or a cap stop occurred (readiness)
q1_closed_loop_oracle_ceiling_nonzero.supported: oracle prevalence over the 24 states > 0 AND the descriptive 95% paired bootstrap interval over the per-state indicators excludes 0 (lower bound > 0; the interval-exclusion rule is the pre-declared practical margin): the closed-loop oracle ceiling is measurably nonzero, so the #85 zero floor is not purely a state-difficulty floor on this membership

q2_ranking_gap_on_ceiling_states.not_supported_by_this_experiment: at least one ceiling state exists and the margin condition is not met after complete execution (the systems select successful candidates too often on this membership for a ranking-gap reading; a valid null)
q2_ranking_gap_on_ceiling_states.prior_arm_role: the no-model ordinal prior arm is REPORTED in the same selection table but is not part of the Q2 margin rule, which is about predictor-guided h=1 ranking
q2_ranking_gap_on_ceiling_states.readiness_or_precision_insufficient: no ceiling state exists (the conditional estimand has empty support), or the decision inventory is incomplete or a cap stop occurred
q2_ranking_gap_on_ceiling_states.supported: at least one ceiling state exists AND every model system (hybrid-fixed-h1, continuous-fixed-h1, continuous-fixed-h5) has a pooled successful-selection rate over ceiling states x 3 seeds < 0.5 AND the pooled-across-model-systems paired descriptive 95% interval over ceiling states lies entirely below 0.5 (the pre-declared numeric margin is 0.5): the systems' h=1 ranking demonstrably misses successful candidates that exist

engine_channel.detection_rule: engine-truth first-shot success is read from the game's own state stream of the executed shot segment (the engine's canonical native fixed-step capture written during rendered play; no parser-derived cost enters the verdict). Primary event leg: pig_removed = the segment records at least one native macro event of type 'pig_removed', 'entity_death' or 'entity_destroyed' with at least one participant whose identity starts 'runtime:pig:' (the game's own pig-removal/death/destruction hooks). structure_destroyed is the same rule over 'runtime:block:' participants. Lifecycle leg (confirmatory): at least one 'runtime:pig:' entity whose per-sample lifecycle in the fixed-step state stream is 'destroyed'. The published verdict is the event leg; the lifecycle leg is published alongside for agreement review against the retained frames
engine_channel.failure_modes: declared failure modes: (1) a death event with an unresolvable participant identity (empty participants) would hide which entity died - detected by the lifecycle leg and typed as a channel anomaly; (2) a pig killed at the very end of the bounded native window may fire its death event before the registry marks the entity destroyed - event leg true with lifecycle leg false is a declared timing mode, recorded, NOT an anomaly; (3) the state stream records a destroyed pig while the event leg is silent - the actual missing-event failure mode - typed as a channel anomaly on that cell; (4) window censoring before any pig death leaves both legs false: the pig survived within the bounded window, not an anomaly
engine_channel.first_shot_success: the executed shot segment's engine-side channel verdict pig_removed; typed failures carry no success value
engine_channel.inheritance: inherited VERBATIM from the published issue-85 engine-truth outcome channel (world_model/training/engine_outcome_reactive_diagnostic.py: CHANNEL_DETECTION_RULE; pig_removed/entity_death/entity_destroyed native macro events with runtime:pig: participants + lifecycle confirmatory leg). The channel was verified with media review in issue-85 Phase A (issue-85 channel-verification.json: verified=true) and is NOT amended by any protocol version of this ticket
engine_channel.shots_to_success: single-shot protocol: 1 when the first shot succeeds, otherwise null; no multi-shot competence claim

definitions.membership_rule: the #80 frozen 24-state membership verbatim (12 type010103 + 12 type010105; identities, inventories, engine seeds and scenario authorities bound by the issue-80 plan file identity); per-state candidate counts are the #80 admissible inventories, which have the #77 typed branch failures removed exactly as recorded (24 x 13 nominal slots - 23 recorded typed drops = 289 oracle candidate slots; the issuing ticket's '~264' is an estimate, the recorded reduction is authoritative)
definitions.oracle_pass: every scheduled (state, admissible candidate) slot is executed exactly once in the real rendered engine from the state's frozen initial condition (source-member decision state at native fixed step 30000), the candidate's frozen action is executed as the single first shot, and engine-truth first-shot success is read with the inherited #85 detection rule; typed failures are retained and carry no success value
definitions.protocol_policy: owner-directed iterative protocol: development versions may be amended after inspecting intermediate results; every version is retained verbatim with a changelog; development outcomes are labelled EXPLORATORY and may not be cited as answers; the terminal version is frozen with actual numeric values BEFORE its own scoring run and executed exactly once

questions.q1_closed_loop_oracle_ceiling_nonzero: on how many of the 24 frozen states does at least one admissible candidate achieve engine-truth first-shot success in closed loop; pooled prevalence with a descriptive interval over states (paired bootstrap, seeds are the single oracle seed)
questions.q2_ranking_gap_on_ceiling_states: conditional on a state having at least one engine-truth-successful candidate, how often does each frozen system select a successful candidate (per seed and pooled, descriptive bootstrap over ceiling states)
